page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate that the instance delivers modest compute performance. Single-core and multi-core CPU tests, including stress-ng and Geekbench, place the processor in the bottom 25% or bottom 10% of performance tiers. However, the system maintains average performance in large-block memory bandwidth read and write operations, as well as Passmark CPU extended instructions. Redis SET operations and small-model LLM inference also perform at average levels, whereas larger model inference and single-threaded compression tasks show weaker results.

From a resource allocation perspective, the ecs.se1.2xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring substantial memory capacity without demanding high-frequency compute power. The tradeoff is evident in the older Intel Xeon architecture, which limits raw processing throughput and single-threaded performance. This makes the instance less suitable for compute-heavy tasks but highly viable for memory-bound applications that benefit from dedicated core allocation and a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio.

This instance is best suited for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high CPU performance or local storage. Appropriate use cases include medium-sized databases, caching layers such as Redis, memory-bound data processing, and general-purpose enterprise applications requiring a larger memory footprint.
